A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NatureLM-audio, with clearly corresponding methods, experiments, and tables. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable Appendices A-G.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, detection, unseen-species, captioning, and individual-counting results in Tables 3-6, plus a speech/music ablation in Section 4.5.

after.justification: v2 reports updated original benchmark results and additional BirdSet, contextual-input, call-transfer, and ablation results in Tables 3-11 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The BEATs/Q-Former/Llama-LoRA architecture and two-stage curriculum remain, but v2 adds full-taxonomy output targets and training conditioned on recording metadata and notes. The reported detection augmentation changes from PCEN/Bird-MixIT/YAMNet processing to environmental-noise mixing, and speech-mixture construction gains time scaling, inserted silence, and reverberation. Appendix B also introduces loss-based classification over allowed labels for BirdSet.

E1.justification: Training coverage changes through LibriTTS/VCTK replacing LibriSpeechD and additions including Barkley Canyon, Clotho, UrbanSound, and noise corpora. Evaluation adds BirdSet, entire-genus/family holdouts, contextual-input scenarios, and multiclass call-type transfer to unseen taxa. Conversely, zebra-finch evaluation narrows from four-way individual counting to distinguishing one bird from multiple birds.

E2.justification: The original main comparator sets remain, but Appendix B/Table 7 substantially expands comparison methods with EffNet, ConvNext, AST, EAT, and W2V2 alongside Perch. Table 5 also adds an explicit theoretical random-chance baseline. These are additions to reported comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: The reported batch size changes from 64 to 128, and speech/music ablation training changes from 200k to 150k steps. Table 2 changes lifestage samples from 493 to 466, call-type samples from 15,439 to 1,000, and zebra-finch samples from 2,346 to 1,160. Holdout construction is revised, while new experiments introduce constrained loss-based BirdSet evaluation and encoder/context controls. Accuracy, macro-F1, and SPIDEr remain the principal metrics.

E4.justification: v1 reports the speech/music ablation only for zebra-finch counting. v2 extends it across BEANS-Zero tasks in Tables 10-11 and adds frozen-versus-unfrozen BEATs controls, metadata/field-note comparisons, and multiclass call-type transfer analyses in Appendices C-F. Species/genus/family comparisons also broaden the investigation of taxonomic distribution shifts.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. v2's additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting; its random-chance baseline is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes all NatureLM-audio scores: for example, ESC50 accuracy rises from 0.635 to 0.820, while HICEAS F1 falls from 0.390 to 0.336, for differently trained models. Table 4 reverses the BirdNET/Perch enabirds scores from 0.164/0.490 to 0.490/0.164. v2 also adds BirdSet, context, transfer, and ablation results. Unseen-taxa and zebra-finch results use revised evaluations and cannot be interpreted as direct gains over v1.

T1.justification: Equation (3) corrects the autoregressive likelihood: v1 predicts the output prefix x_<t, whereas v2 predicts y_t conditioned on the instruction, audio representation, and previous output tokens. This is a limited mathematical correction, without new theorems or proofs or evidence that the implemented loss changed.

C1.justification: The principal first-model, state-of-the-art, zero-shot generalization, and speech/music-transfer claims remain. v2's abstract modestly expands the claimed resource contribution to released model weights and benchmark data, beyond the code emphasized in v1.

C2.justification: v2 refines the generalization interpretation: full taxonomic names help across holdout levels, while scientific names can underperform common names on unseen genera. It adds interpretations concerning contextual information and the importance of encoder fine-tuning, and removes v1's mosquito-wingbeat failure explanation. The overarching transfer interpretation and ethical limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the BEATs checkpoint, LLM initialization, LoRA placement/rank/alpha/dropout, learning-rate endpoint, and main-stage training budgets. Appendix A lists held-out taxa, and Figure 3 documents training-prompt composition. The abstract reports released weights and benchmark data, and the pending-code-release footnote disappears. These substantial disclosures should not all be interpreted as changes to previously used settings; external availability is not established by the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: The central research positioning remains, with additions including BirdSet and Sarkar and Magimai-Doss's speech-to-animal-caller work. v2 connects taxonomic naming to the already cited BioCLIP and updates citations for changed data/preprocessing. The introduction replaces the assertion that BirdNET/Perch generalize poorly beyond birds with a distinction about requiring dedicated classifiers. Publication-metadata updates do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and technical explanations receive extensive prose editing. v1's unified Methods section becomes separate training-data, evaluation-data, architecture, and training-method sections; non-bioacoustic data descriptions are regrouped. Contributions are reformatted, authorship expands, and v2 adds an organized appendix structure with a contents list.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different page design with a wider text area, branding, and revised heading/caption typography. Tables 1-2 change their displayed coverage, and Table 5 is expanded and reorganized around three holdout levels and naming variants. Five new result tables and the training-data sunburst in Figure 3 substantially extend the visual presentation; Figures 1-2 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited validation and reproducibility: deeper taxonomic holdouts, call-transfer tests, encoder/context controls, full-task ablation reporting, and explicit implementation and held-out-taxon details make the central generalization claims more assessable. These gains are substantive, independent of higher reported scores. Replacing four-way counting with a binary task weakens that particular evidence, the Table 4 score reversal is unexplained, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. Nevertheless, the broader controlled evidence and documentation provide a clear overall improvement.
